2161.sol: Non sense codon or terminator codon are the codons that do not code for any amino acid. 3334.sol: Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative on moving down a group due to increase in atomic size. 55886.text: Which statement from following is correct for hemolytic fission?
options: In this single electron of shared pair moves to one of bonded atom and other to other atom.
In this electron deficient and electron rich species are formed.
In this electronegative atom pulls both electrons of shared pair.
In this carbon free radical formed has sp ^3 hybridisation.
55886.sol: Homolytic fission (sometimes referred to as hemolysis) is a type of bond fission that involves the dissociation of a given molecule wherein one electron is retained by each of the original fragments of the molecule. Therefore, when a neutrally charged molecule is subjected to homolytic fission, two free radicals are obtained as the product (since each of the chemical species retains one electron from the bond pair).

71489.subject: Biology
71489.text: Match type of outbreeding device given in Column I with respective example given in Column II Column (I) Column (II) (A) Protogyny (I) Calotropis (B) Herkogamy (II) Primula (C) Self sterility (III) Gloriosa (D) Heterostyly (IV) Thea Choose the correct option

A - III, B - I, C - II, D - IV
A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
71489.sol: Protogyny is a condition where the stigma matures earlier than the anthers, preventing self-pollination. An example is Gloriosa . Herkogamy refers to the presence of a physical barrier between the anthers and stigma of the same flower, as seen in Calotropis . Self sterility or self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules. An example is Thea . Heterostyly is the presence of different lengths of styles and stamens in flowers of the same species, such as in Primula

72032.text: Which of the following statements regarding spontaneous process is NOT true?
options: It proceeds in both directions even in absence of external stimulant.
Spontaneity is not concerned with rate of reaction.
It continues till equilibrium is reached.
72032.sol: A spontaneous process is one that occurs on its own without any external assistance. It is a unidirectional process, meaning it proceeds only in one direction under a given set of conditions. It cannot proceed in the reverse direction without the help of an external agency. Therefore, it does not proceed in both directions. Thermodynamics determines the spontaneity of a process but provides no information about the rate of the reaction (kinetics). 79359.subject: Botany
79359.text: Large, empty colourless cells of the adaxial epidermis along the veins of grass leaves are:
79359.sol: In monocots like grass, the upper epidermis or adaxial surface has a motor or bulliform cells. These cells are large, empty colourless cells and are present along the veins. These cells by osmotic changes help in the rolling and unrolling of leaf lamina, which regulates the rate of transpiration.

80101.subject: Botany
80101.text: In Bougainvillea , thorns are the modifications of:
80101.sol: Thorns are hard, pointed straight structures for protection. These are modified stem. Thorns represent the modification of an axillary shoot system in which the leaves are reduced and die quickly and the stems are heavily sclerified and grow for only a limited time. They help in providing protection.

80304.subject: Botany
80304.text: Opening of floral buds into flowers, is a type of:
80304.sol: The opening of floral buds and the change into a flower is a nastic movement. It is a type of autonomic movement of growth in which the direction of the movement isindependent of the direction of the stimulus. In fact, the response is determined by the structure of the responsive organ and not by the opposite side. 80521.subject: Botany
80521.text: The viability of seeds is tested by:
80521.sol: Viability of seeds can be known by two methods: (i) ability to germinate, (ii) testing their ability to respire. All viable seeds respire. This can be tested by immersing a section of seed containing the embryo in 0.1 % solution of triphenyl tetrazolium chloride. The viable embryo will turn pink due to conversion of colourless triphenyl tetrazolium chloride into insoluble coloured dye called triphenyl formazone due to reduction. Tetrazolium Chloride (TZ) test is also called as quick germination test. Related Theory

84065.text: Which of the following is associated with decrease in cardiac output?
84065.sol: The sympathetic nerve ending releases noradrenaline which stimulates the SAN that accelerates the heartbeat, the strength of ventricular contraction and thereby the cardiac output. 84166.subject: Zoology
84166.text: Reduction in pH of blood will:
options: Reduce the rate of heart beat
Reduce the blood supply to the brain
Decrease the affinity of haemoglobin with oxygen
Release bicarbonate ions by the liver
84166.sol: A rise in the pCO 2 or fall in pH(High H + ion concentration) decreases oxygen affinity of haemoglobin, raising the P 50 value. This is called Bohr effect. Decrease in pH increases acidity of the blood that results in dissociation of oxygen and Hb which occurs in the body tissues.

84189.sol: Residual air is the air which remains in the lungs after the most forceful expiration. It is about 1200 ml . As the residual air remains in the lungs, it has no effect on respiration efficiency.

84844.sol: Both statements are correct. The process of copying genetic information from one strand of the DNA into RNA is termed as transcription. A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in the DNA i.e. a promoter, the structural gene and a terminator.

85083.subject: Zoology
85083.text: Assertion (A): A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations. Reason (R): Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygen. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
85083.sol: Altitude sickness (AMS) is experienced by a person at a high altitude where the body does not get enough oxygen due to low atmospheric pressure and causes nausea, fatigue and heart palpitations. Under these conditions, the body increases RBC production, decreases the binding capacity of haemoglobin and increases breathing rate. These physiological adaptations allow organisms to respond quickly to stressful conditions.

100013.subject: Physics
100013.text: A student measures human body temperature by placing a thermometer under the armpit. This method always gives a temperature reading that is lower than the actual internal body temperature. 100013.sol: According to NCERT, measuring temperature under the armpit will always give a reading lower than the actual body temperature. This is a consistent error occurring in one direction due to a flawed procedure, which falls under the category of systematic errors, specifically termed as 'imperfection in experimental technique or procedure'. It is not an instrumental error because the thermometer itself may be perfectly calibrated. It is not a personal error because it is not caused by individual carelessness or parallax

102882.subject: Physics
102882.text: The magnitude of the electric field E of a spherically symmetric charge distribution varies with the distance r from its centre. The graph of E versus r shows that E increases linearly from zero at r=0 to a maximum value E₀ at r=R , and then decreases for r > R . A point charge q is moved slowly from the centre ( r=0 ) to the surface ( r=R ) along a random curved path. What is the magnitude of the work done by the ex
102882.sol: The electrostatic field is conservative, meaning the work done in moving a charge is independent of the path taken and depends only on the initial and final positions. The work done by an external agent in moving a charge q slowly is given by W = q V , where V is the potential difference between the final and initial points. The magnitude of the potential difference | V| between r=0 and r=R is equal to the magnitude of the line integral of the electric field, which corresponds to the area under the E versus r graph

103131.sol: The equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination of C₁ and C₂ is: C₁₂ = C + C = 2C This combination is connected in series with C₃ (capacitance C ) across the voltage source V . The voltage across the parallel combination (which is the voltage across C₁ ) is: V₁ = V C₃ C₁₂ + C₃ = V C 2C + C = V 3 The voltage across C₃ is: V₃ = V C₁₂ C₁₂ + C₃ = V 2C 2C + C = 2V 3 The energy stored in capacitor C₁ is: U₁ = 1 2 C₁ V₁^2 = 1 2 C ( V 3 )^2 = CV^

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
104019.sol: The reactance of a circuit containing a capacitor and an inductor is given by X = X L - X C = ω L - 1 ω C . An AC circuit has zero reactance at resonance, i.e., when, X L = X C . The power consumption in an AC circuit is zero when circuit contains only inductance or capacitance since average power consumed in a cycle is zero for inductance or capacitance. So, second statement is false.

106404.sol: According to Bohr's model, the radius of the n^ th orbit is given by: r_n = a₀ n^2 Z For the second orbit of He ⁺ ( n=2, Z=2 ): r_ He ^+ = a₀ 2^2 2 = 2a₀ = 105.8 pm For the n^ th orbit of Be ³⁺ ( Z=4 ): r_ Be ³⁺ = a₀ n^2 4 = 211.6 pm Taking the ratio of the two radii: r_ Be ³⁺ r_ He ^+ = a₀ n^2 4 2a₀ = n^2 8 Substitute the given values: 211.6 105.8 = n^2 8 2 = n^2 8 n^2 = 16 n = 4 The principal quantum number is 4 . 128602.sol: Normal ovulation requires a mid-cycle LH surge, which is triggered by a peak in natural estrogen (positive feedback). When a female takes oral contraceptive pills, the continuous exogenous supply of estrogen and progestogen maintains a constant negative feedback on the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary. This negative feedback inhibits the release of gonadotropins (FSH and LH). Without the LH surge, the Graafian follicle does not rupture, and ovulation is successfully prevented. options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
128624.sol: The secretion of the posterior lobe of pituitary is known as pituitrin and it contains two hormones. (i) Oxytocin or pitocin. (ii) Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin. The posterior lobe of the pituitary gland does not secrete any hormone. Its hormones are secreted in the hypothalamus. 128774.subject: Zoology
128774.text: What is the colour of the plasma?
128774.sol: Explanation : Plasma is a straw coloured , viscous fluid constituting nearly 55 per cent of the blood. 90-92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6-8 per cent of it. Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins are the major proteins.

128882.subject: Zoology
128882.text: What causes the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves during ventricular systole?
options: The opening of the semilunar valves
The flow of blood in the ventricles
The closure of the semilunar valves
128882.sol: Ventricular systole increases the ventricular pressure causing the closure of tricuspid and bicuspid valves due to attempted backflow of blood into the atria. As the ventricular pressure increases further, the semilunar valves guarding the pulmonary artery (right side) and the aorta (left side) are forced open, allowing the blood in the ventricles to flow through these vessels into the circulatory pathways.

129096.text: Which of the following represents the action of insulin?
options: Increases blood glucose level by stimulating glucagon production.
Decreases blood glucose level by forming glycogen.
Increases blood glucose level by promoting cellular uptake of glucose.
Increases blood glucose level by hydrolysis of glycogen.
129096.sol: Insulin decreases the level of glucose in the blood. It acts by stimulating liver cells and muscle cells to take up glucose from the blood and convert it into glycogen. When the blood sugar level drops, the secretion of insulin is suppressed. When the blood sugar level increases, the secretion of insulin is stimulated.

132523.sol: Thalassemia and sickle-cell anaemia are both autosomal recessive blood disorders. However, thalassemia is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules, whereas sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin. 132579.sol: Haemophilia is a blood disorder where the blood does not clot normally. Haemophilia A is the most common form, caused by a deficiency of blood clotting factor VIII. 95892.sol: The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans. In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight. options: It undergoes transamination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to form glumate acid which further undergoes reductiv
It undergoes reductive amination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumatine which further undergoes transaminat
It undergoes transamination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumatine which further undergoes reductive aminat
It undergoes reductive amination with alpha ketoglutaric acid to glumate which further undergoes transaminatio
96755.sol: At physiological pH, the ammonia is protonated to form (ammonium) ion. (i) Reductive amination : In these processes, ammonium ion reacts with α-ketoglutaric acid and forms glutamic acid. (ii) Transamination : It involves the transfer of amino group from one amino acid to the keto group of a keto acid. Glutamic acid is the main amino acid from which the transfer of NH2, the amino group takes place and other amino acids are formed through transamination. The enzyme transaminase catalyses all such reactions.

98484.text: Which of the following is not a nucleoside?
98484.sol: Purine and pyrimidine nucleotides polymerize to form nucleic acids. Adenosine, guanosine, thymidine, uridine and cytidine are nucleosides. Nicotinamide and riboflavin nucleotides act as coenzymes of oxidizing enzymes. A nucleoside is formed by the nitrogenous base and pentose sugar. DNA nucleosides are known as deoxyribose nucleosides while RNA nucleosides are known as ribose nucleosides. Adenylic acid, thymidylic acid, guanylic acid, uridylic acid and cytidylic acid are nucleotides.

304046.text: A steel wire and a copper wire, both possessing equal length and equal cross-sectional area, are joined end to end and the combination is subjected to a tension. 304046.sol: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area. When the wires are joined end to end and subjected to a tension, they are in a series combination. 304399.subject: Physics
304399.text: When viewed from an inertial frame of reference, a particle of mass m is seen travelling in a circle of radius r at a uniform speed v . What is the centrifugal force acting on the particle?
options: mv^2 r directed away from the centre
mv^2 r along the tangent passing through the particle
mv^2 r directed towards the centre
304399.sol: Centrifugal force is a pseudo force which is experienced only in a non-inertial (rotating) frame of reference. When viewed from an inertial frame of reference, no pseudo forces are present. The particle executes circular motion solely due to a real centripetal force of magnitude mv^2 r directed towards the centre. Thus, the centrifugal force acting on the particle in an inertial frame is zero.

305727.subject: Physics
305727.text: Using a 20 W heater, a metal ball of mass 1 kg is heated inside a room that is maintained at 20^ C . The ball's temperature eventually settles at a steady value of 50^ C . Determine the rate of loss of heat to the surrounding when the ball is at 50^ C .
305727.sol: At steady state, the temperature of the metal ball becomes constant, which implies that the net rate of heat transfer is zero. The rate of heat supplied by the heater must be exactly equal to the rate of heat lost by the ball to the surroundings. Given that the power of the heater is 20 W , the rate of heat supplied is 20 J/s . Therefore, the rate of loss of heat to the surroundings at the steady temperature of 50^ C is 20 W .

6a7a1ff88a9b6148180d7e07.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff88a9b6148180d7e07.text: Consider the following physical phenomena: A. Compton scattering B. X-ray diffraction C. Blackbody radiation D. Resolving power of an electron microscope Which of the given phenomena provide direct evidence for the particle nature of electromagnetic radiation?
6a7a1ff88a9b6148180d7e07.sol: Compton scattering involves the collision between a photon and an electron, which can only be explained by treating electromagnetic radiation as particles (photons). Blackbody radiation requires the assumption that energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete quanta, supporting the particle nature of radiation. X-ray diffraction is a phenomenon that relies on the wave nature of electromagnetic radiation. The resolving power of an electron microscope is based on the wave nature of matter (De Broglie waves of electrons)

6a7a1ff84315d7386d54dea7.text: For hydrogen-like species, a graph of the square root of the magnitude of total energy ( |E_n| ) versus atomic number ( Z ) is plotted for two different principal quantum numbers, n=2 and n=3 . Both plots yield straight lines passing through the origin. What is the ratio of the slope of the line for n=2 to the slope of the line for n=3 ?
6a7a1ff84315d7386d54dea7.sol: The energy of the n^ th stationary state for a hydrogen-like species is: E_n = -13.6 Z^2 n^2 eV The magnitude of the energy is: |E_n| = 13.6 Z^2 n^2 Taking the square root on both sides: |E_n| = 13.6 n Z This represents a straight line equation y = mZ passing through the origin, where the slope m = 13.6 n . Thus, the slope is inversely proportional to n ( m 1 n ). The ratio of the slopes for n=2 and n=3 is: m_ n=2 m_ n=3 = 1 2 1 3 = 3 2 Therefore, the ratio is 3 : 2 . Answer: 3 : 2
